text:
maria: quick heads-up — bringing up Aurelia-13B (Gemma-derivative) on int4. Seeing two strange things: 1) tokenizer is splitting combining diacritics into separate tokens (e.g. "e\u0301" -> 'e' + combining), 2) rotary frequency per-head looks nonuniform after quant; some heads show ~0.6x frequency. reproducible on small prompt.
kevin: can you paste the convert command + tokenizer config? also which quant tool?
mania: (typo) maria — command: `python convert_model.py --src=gemma/aurelia.ckpt --out=ggml-aurelia-int4.bin --quant=int4` + export flags. Tokenizer config excerpt: "do_normalize": false, "split_on_whitespace": false. Sample tokens for "Café": [101, 2048, 13723, 3] (expected single token for "é").
anand: that token split is suspicious — we normally run NFKC/NFC normalization during ingest. Is the tokenizer upstream or from model repo?
maria: tokenizer came with model repo (they shipped their own). I didn't run lexnorm. attaching tiny dump of token->string: `72 -> C`, `2048 -> a`, `13723 -> \u0301` (combining acute).
julie: for the rotary issue — how are you measuring frequency? simple vector angle check?
maria: quick check: for each head i compute normalized dot between pos_embed[t] after rotary for head i and expected sin/cos pattern. Some heads' phase slope is visibly lower. small snippet: ```python
# quick rotary slope check
for h in range(n_heads):
    v0 = pos_enc[h, :100]
    v1 = pos_enc[h, 1:101]
    slope = np.mean(np.angle(np.fft.fft(v1)) - np.angle(np.fft.fft(v0)))
    print(h, slope)
```
kevin: hmmm could be a packing bug during per-head quant scale fold. Did convert_model fold rotary freqs into int8-scale table?
maria: convert_model has a headwise scaling pass to save bandwidth. I skipped unit tests. reproducer: `echo "The quick brown fox" | python run_infer.py --model ggml-aurelia-int4.bin --tokens 64` yields visible drift in long-context token similarity compared to float32 baseline.
ci-bot: ci/test-onboard-aurelia triggered — status: flaky, 2/5 failures (tokenization/regression test). See: https://ci.redwood/9876
anand: immediate triage plan: 1) rerun tokenizer with NFC normalization (pre-tokenize) and see if combining marks collapse; 2) rerun convert with headwise-rotary-force-uniform flag (disable per-head scaling) to confirm. can you run both and paste diffs?
maria: running NFC prenorm now + quick convert with `--rotary-uniform` flag. will post outputs in a min.
julie: also add a short eval: summarize 10 news articles with both bins (float vs int4) and compare rouge/QA answer exact match, just to quantify quality hit.
maria: quick results: NFC fixed token split — "Café" tokens now [101, 2048, 13723_combined, 3] (single token). rotary-uniform convert removed frequency variance — cosine similarity on longctx rises from 0.72 -> 0.95 vs fp32. rouge delta ~ -0.7 on original int4, after uniform flag delta ~ -0.1.
kevin: good signal. Sounds like 2 independent fixes: normalize tokenizer input and avoid per-head rotary scaling in quant pass. For shipping: prefer tokenizer change as permanent; for quant, add guard and per-model opt-in.
anand: agreed. action items: maria to open PR to upstream tokenizer to enable NFC by default (and add unit test), kevin to patch convert_model to make per-head rotary scaling opt-in and add regression tests, julie to run a broader eval suite (200 examples) and report.
maria: opening PRs now, will link. thanks. :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: PRs created: #243-tokenizer-nfc, #244-rotary-quant-uniform. CI: running full eval (ETA ~45m).
kevin: nice. anyone wants oncall review for the convert patch? @anand?
anand: I'll take it.
maria: closing loop — learned: check unicode combining marks + avoid opaque headwise freq folding in quant. saved a painful drift. :relieved:
